articles.title: India's Chess Olympiad medallist Nihal Sarin replies to 'play for Pakistan' troll with three words
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Indian grandmaster Nihal Sarin didn't need more than three words to shut down a troll on X.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Indian grandmaster Nihal Sarin didn't need more than three words to shut down a troll on X. After India's open team wrapped up their campaign at the 46th Chess Olympiad in Samarkand with a silver medal, Nihal posted a simple message of celebration, penning, "Happy to win silver for Team India. Congratulations to Uzbekistan."It should have been an uncontroversial post. Instead, it drew an ugly reply from one user. "Plz quit playing for India. Play for Pakistan," the comment read, which has now been deleted.Nihal didn't let it slide, nor did he engage at length. His response was just as brief as the provocation. The Kerala-born grandmaster wrote, "on board 0?"At Chess Olympiad, players are assigned to boards 1 through 4 based on rating/strength within the squad, with Board 1 being the strongest player. As for example, Nihal was on Board 3 for India at this Chess Olympiad. There's no such thing as "Board 0". Nihal’s “on board 0?” was a sarcastic, understated way of turning the jab on its head. The implication was that if he were playing for Pakistan, he, currently rated 2718, would be so far ahead of the team’s existing board order that even Board 1 would not be enough, hence the tongue-in-cheek invention of “Board 0”.Rather than engage with the provocation, Nihal dismissed it in three words.A mixed personal campaignThe exchange came at the end of a tournament that had its own share of ups and downs for the 22-year-old chess star individually.He started in fine form, winning his first three games, against Thailand, Indonesia and Italy, before the results cooled off with back-to-back draws against Spain and the Netherlands.Round 6, against hosts Uzbekistan, proved to be the turning point. Nihal blundered his queen in a winning position against Nodirbek Yakubboev, a loss that visibly rattled him, he lost again the very next round, in a marathon 88-move battle against England's Luke McShane.Those two defeats were the only blemishes on an otherwise solid campaign; Nihal steadied himself in the rounds that followed, drawing against Germany's Frederik Svane, beating Uzbekistan second team's Mukhammadzokhid Suyarov in Round 10, and closing out the tournament with a draw against Hungary's Benjamin Gledura.The individual numbers, though, were always going to matter less than the team result. India's open side secured silver behind hosts Uzbekistan.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Just two plates for Virat Kohli: How Anushka Sharma’s chole bhature search transformed a struggling Mumbai shop into a Rs20 million-a-month business
articles.summary: A small chole bhature shop in Mumbai that was once preparing to shut down after piling up nearly Rs1.8 million in debt is now serving around 3,000 plates
articles.body: A small chole bhature shop in Mumbai that was once preparing to shut down after piling up nearly Rs1.8 million in debt is now serving around 3,000 plates a day and claims to generate nearly Rs20 million in monthly sales.For Delhi Se, a tiny 250-square-foot outlet in Chembur, the remarkable turnaround began with an unexpected Instagram recommendation from stand-up comedian Abhishek Upmanyu and eventually involved an order from Anushka Sharma’s home for Virat Kohli.The business was being run by brothers Jaspal Singh Khalsa and Mahinder Singh Khalsa, who had just three tables and nine seats at their outlet. Things had started going downhill in January 2022, and by September, the brothers were carrying nearly Rs1.8 million in debt.“We were planning to close the restaurant,” Jaspal told Pinkvilla.The brothers were preparing to settle their outstanding grocery bills and rent before shutting the shop for good. Then, on September 13, 2022, an unexpected customer walked through the door.The Instagram story that changed everythingStand-up comedian Abhishek Upmanyu visited the Chembur outlet, tried its chole bhature and recommended the food on Instagram.At the time, the brothers did not know who he was.“We didn’t know him then. On September 14 and 15, our walk-ins started increasing,” Jaspal recalled.That recommendation would soon lead to something far bigger.The Instagram post eventually reached Anushka Sharma, who was looking for authentic Delhi-style chole bhature in Mumbai for Virat Kohli.Before Anushka publicly spoke about the restaurant, however, the brothers began receiving repeated calls from a woman claiming to be from her home. She wanted two plates delivered to Juhu and also asked for the restaurant’s bank details.Jaspal thought something was wrong.“I told Mahinder, ‘This woman is troubling me. She has called eight times and is asking for my bank details.’ Mahinder said, ‘What’s the problem? Give her the bank details.’ I said, ‘What if she hacks the account?’ Mahinder replied, ‘The account balance is already negative. There is hardly any money in it,’” Jaspal recalled.After several calls, the brothers finally learnt that the order was genuinely from Virat Kohli’s home.Even then, Jaspal struggled to believe it.“I said, ‘Ma’am, please don’t say things like that. Where is Virat Kohli and where am I – a small chole bhature shop in Chembur? How am I supposed to believe that you’re calling from Virat Kohli’s house?’” Jaspal said.Anushka Sharma post brings an instant crowdThe mystery was soon cleared up when Anushka posted on Instagram that she had finally found “ekdum-Delhi-jaise-Chole-bhature” in Mumbai. She also credited Upmanyu for pointing her towards the eatery.The response was almost instantaneous.“After her post, there was a massive crowd at the restaurant. Within half an hour, such a huge crowd had gathered that we were completely blank,” Jaspal said.The three-table outlet suddenly found itself dealing with a rush it was nowhere near equipped to handle. Customers started placing orders for six or even 10 plates at a time, while the restaurant rapidly ran out of stock.The crowd outside became so large that police reportedly arrived at the spot.With demand far exceeding their preparations, the brothers began sourcing soaked chickpeas from neighbours to keep the kitchen running. Some customers reportedly waited for more than two hours to get just two or three plates.The scale of the operation changed dramatically within days. According to Jaspal, the quantity of chole being prepared increased from around 8kg to 100kg within three days.From a nine-seat shop to four outletsThe sudden attention turned what was once a struggling neighbourhood outlet into the foundation of a much larger business.Delhi Se has since expanded from the original Chembur shop to four outlets spread across Mumbai and Navi Mumbai.The owners now claim that the brand sells approximately 3,000 plates of chole bhature every day. Around 125kg of chickpeas are soaked daily, with the quantity increasing significantly after cooking.The financial numbers have changed just as dramatically.When the business was struggling, monthly sales were around Rs100,000–150,000 and the brothers were barely breaking even. Today, they claim monthly sales of approximately Rs20 million.What began as a tiny nine-seat restaurant preparing to close was transformed by a chain of events the brothers could hardly have anticipated: a comedian’s Instagram recommendation, a search for authentic Delhi-style chole bhature and an order from Virat Kohli’s home.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Savitha Shri’s Chess Olympiad gold demands a closer look beyond the stunning 9/10
articles.summary: Savitha Shri’s individual gold medal performance (9 points in 10 games) is a highly notable achievement.
articles.body: Savitha Shri’s individual gold medal performance (9 points in 10 games) is a highly notable achievement. Her exploits at the Chess Olympiad that concluded in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, on Sunday, however, warrant a closer look.“I really don't know what to say... for gambling the positions or keeping us tense throughout the rounds! But yes, when there were really tense moments, she was strong enough to capitalise on those opportunities. She has the fighting spirit and she is not scared of playing any position. Irrespective of the evaluation, she keeps fighting,” India’s top board player Koneru Humpy told the Chessbase India webcast about Savitha Shri.In other words, those were not simply clean wins where she outplayed her opponents. The majority of the games featured multiple inaccuracies, which is the norm in shorter time controls but not in classical chess.Veteran GM Levon Aronian told Lichess in an interview that if players want to win, they will have to take gambles these days as the level of preparation has increased. There is, however, a thin line between taking risks and being in reasonable control despite taking liberties.It is also unclear if Savitha Shri was fully aware of the dangers of her inaccuracies. Savitha Shri, 19, also played on the reserve board (fifth). Despite slipping from the Elo high of 2435 four years ago to 2382 at this Olympiad, all her rivals were lower-rated than her.Still, the value of IM Savitha Shri’s performance for India cannot be ignored. She scored eight wins when GMs K Humpy, R Vaishali and Divya Deshmukh scored a combined nine wins.Vaishali (2.5/6) was rested for four of the last seven rounds. Her form is a huge worry as she is expected to challenge China’s Ju Wenjun for the women’s world crown early next year.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Senate passes college sports bill that would rein in athlete payments and transfers
articles.summary: The overwhelming 77-22 vote to pass the legislation is Congress’ strongest effort yet to set national regulations governing payments to college athletes for their names, images and likenesses and how often they can transfer.
articles.body: The Senate passed a sweeping bipartisan bill on Monday that would regulate college sports, an attempt to end “chaos” in an industry that has been upended by skyrocketing athlete payments and near-unrestricted transfers between schools. The overwhelming 77-22 vote to pass the legislation is the strongest effort yet by Congress to set national regulations governing payments to college athletes for their names, images and likenesses and how often they can transfer. It would give the NCAA new authority over those rules and limited antitrust protections to enforce them. The bill is the product of years of Senate negotiations that intensified after a 2025 lawsuit settlement uprooted the college sports landscape by allowing colleges to pay their players. The legislation, which would still have to pass the House, would codify the settlement into law but also establish new guardrails around the system in an attempt to rein in the runaway costs for colleges. “It would be nice if college sports could somehow magically fix itself, but this is a matter of law, federal law, and only Congress can fix it,” said Senate Commerce Committee Chairman Ted Cruz, R-Texas, who negotiated the bill with the top Democrat on the panel, Sen. Maria Cantwell of Washington. The bill’s backers — more than 70 senators from both parties — say it aims to curtail constant litigation and uncertainty across college sports for athletes, schools and fans. It would also give hundreds of thousands of student-athletes new health and labor protections. But critics say the bill doesn’t do enough to protect athletes or curtail the enormous sums of money flowing to coaches, colleges and conferences. “This is a bill that essentially ensconces a system of exploitation, and it doesn’t fix the broader problems,” said Sen. Chris Murphy of Connecticut, a Democrat who has worked with labor and civil rights groups to rally opposition to the bill. The bill’s future is still unclear. President Donald Trump has repeatedly expressed an interest in the legislation, and the White House formally endorsed the bill last month. But it could face an uphill battle in the House, which failed repeatedly over the last year to get a different version to the floor and is in recess until after the November elections. Lawmakers will have to start over in the next Congress if the bill doesn’t pass both chambers by the end of the year. Bill addresses skyrocketing spending, unlimited transfers College sports have been reeling in the wake of the 2025 court settlement allowing colleges to directly pay players for their name, image and likeness. The fallout has reshaped the industry and led to football roster payrolls that can exceed $40 million. The bill would codify the court settlement, including a revenue cap that allows schools to share up to $21.5 million in revenue with their players. The legislation would more than double that amount for some schools, allowing up to an additional $27.5 million in payments through a retention fund — a change that helped win the support of the two largest conferences, the Big Ten and Southeastern Conference. To help schools raise more revenue, the bill would give schools and conferences the option of pooling their TV media rights. The legislation also aims to stabilize the NCAA transfer portal that has led to players constantly switching teams. It would restrict player transfers to one “free” move over five years without sitting out a year, with some exceptions, and also would restrict players to five years of total eligibility. The proposed eligibility limit comes amid backlash to schools that have increasingly pushed boundaries, including LSU’s now-canceled plans to place players on the roster who had participated in NFL training camps. “That was probably like a big lamp for some people who saw it and said, ‘Oh my God, this is so out of control,’” Cantwell said in a recent interview with The Associated Press. The bill also would restrict coaches from leaving their schools during the season, force schools that want to switch conferences to spend three years as an independent and prevent conferences from growing larger than 20 programs — an effort to prevent so-called superleagues from taking over sports. A last-minute amendment proposed by Sen. Ashley Moody of Florida raised that cap from 19 in the original legislation. The vote was delayed several hours on Monday as senators negotiated Moody’s amendment and others that were eventually adopted, including provisions to make it easier for athletes to sue over sexual assault and a requirement to disclose foreign financing. The Senate rejected an amendment by Sen. John Kennedy, R-La., that would have put limits on ticket prices for fans and two by Sen. Cory Booker, D-N.J., that would have capped coaches’ salaries at $5 million a year and increased compensation for athletes who have catastrophic injuries. Critics say it wouldn’t do enough to help athletes The legislation includes new protections for athletes, including caps on agent fees and guarantees for health insurance and scholarships. It would also require schools to maintain a minimum number of sports and roster spots — an effort to ensure that women’s and Olympic sports are not cut in favor of football, basketball and other sports that generate more revenue. Still, some Democrats say it wouldn’t do enough to limit the big money in college sports. The legislation “places a cap on the students’ cut of the revenues, but there are no caps on coaches’ salaries or on the size of donations to athletic programs,” Murphy said last week. Groups like the NAACP, the Congressional Black Caucus and the AFL-CIO have also opposed the bill, in part, because it leaves unresolved whether athletes should be considered employees with the ability to collectively bargain. All four Black Democrats in the Senate — Booker, Raphael Warnock of Georgia, Lisa Blunt Rochester of Delaware and Angela Alsobrooks of Maryland — have opposed the bill. Booker, who played football at Stanford in the late 1980s on a scholarship, noted the “outsized role” that Black athletes play in college sports. He said it wasn’t until college athletes were able to begin to win cases in court that the power started to shift, “and now the NCAA is coming here to the United States Senate, asking for sweeping powers” to exempt antitrust laws. “We know who this bill is protecting,” Booker said. House passage is uncertain Despite strong bipartisan support in the Senate, the bill faces a murky path in the House. House lawmakers won’t return to Washington until mid-November, after the elections. And it’s unclear what will be on Republican leaders’ agenda in the chaotic last few weeks of the session. Pressure from Trump could help push the bill to passage. But some House Republicans have insisted on language explicitly stating that athletes are not employees, which the Senate bill does not have — a key concession to Cantwell to win enough Democratic support.

articles.title: Rain ruins India’s Asian Games cricket quarterfinal, fans left with ‘far-off view’ of players
articles.summary: Nisshin: Handshakes between the teams.
articles.body: Nisshin: Handshakes between the teams. That was the only action possible at the Korogi Sports Park in Nisshin on Monday as persistent rain forced both Asian Games cricket quarterfinals to be abandoned without a ball being bowled.Despite most of the outfield being covered, the surface remained wet and, with no sign of the sun, officials had little option but to call off the matches before the toss.India and Pakistan advanced to their respective semifinals by virtue of being the higher-ranked teams. For the sizable number of Indian fans who had travelled from different parts of Japan hoping to watch their team in action, it was a major disappointment.Rahil Yadav, who lives in Kyoto, said he had taken a chance despite the weather.“Given the weather for the past few days, I knew it was unlikely that the match would happen, but I was just being hopeful because for us Indians living here, it was a great opportunity to watch our team in action. But all we managed was a far-off view of the players,” he rued.Japan Cricket Association COO and high-performance director Alan Curr told TOI that the national federation was disappointed despite the efforts that had gone into preparing the stadium for the Games.“It is disappointing. It was hard to get things up and running here. That said, there is nothing we can do and weather is a big part of cricket. The rain is a bit unseasonable because in Sept last year it was warm and sunny. The typhoons usually blow over and we hoped the weather would hold up. We have lost three matches in a row now. We can only hope for the weather to get better,” the Englishman said.India’s semifinal opponent will depend on the outcome of the Nepal-Sri Lanka quarterfinal, scheduled for Tuesday. If that match goes ahead, India will face the winner on Thursday. Should it be washed out, Sri Lanka will advance on the basis of their higher ranking.Before the team left for the venue, they were greeted by Indian Olympic Association president and athletics legend PT Usha at the hotel.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: WWE RAW Results & Highlights 28-September-2026: Oba Femi addresses The Vision, IYO SKY vs. Lyra Valkyria, The Bloodline promo and more
articles.summary: WWE Raw came to Milwaukee's Fiserv Forum on Monday, September 28, 2026, and it began quietly.
articles.body: WWE Raw came to Milwaukee's Fiserv Forum on Monday, September 28, 2026, and it began quietly. A video remembered Benjamin Satterley, known to fans as Neville who tragically passes away on Sunday, September 27, 2026, before the show shifted to a card packed with grudges.Oba Femi walked out with a Money in the Bank contract in hand, and IYO SKY was handed a tough test in Lyra Valkyria. The Bloodline spent the night hunting for 946 after the abduction of Solo Sikoa, and Dragon Lee found himself in a hard fight with Big Cass.The Bloodline promo on 946Jey Uso, Jimmy Uso and Jacob Fatu opened the show without World Heavyweight Champion Roman Reigns. Jimmy said the family had been beaten down and had a car blown up weeks ago, but the abduction of Solo Sikoa was a step too far. Fatu took the blame for his earlier push to stay patient, then said patience was over. When 946's SUV pulled in, the group charged the garage and attacked a stagehand, only to stop when NXT's Jaida Parker stepped out asking for Adam Pearce.Lola Vice vs. Roxanne PerezLola Vice and Roxanne Perez started with side headlocks and arm drags under referee Jessika Carr. Perez took over outside the ring, driving Vice into the commentary table and steel steps before hitting a northern lights suplex on the floor. Vice used her MMA training to counter a crossface into a triangle choke, and Perez escaped with a roll-up for a two-count. A spinning back fist ended it for Vice. Women's Intercontinental Champion Raquel Rodriguez then attacked her, Sol Ruca's save fell short, and Perez finished the beatdown with Pop Rox.Winner: Lola ViceOba Femi promo on The VisionThe crowd chanted "Oba," and The Ruler told them to settle down. Femi said he was dressed for business, not combat, though that could change. He admitted Bronson Reed's return had shifted the mood around The Vision, then held up a Money in the Bank contract approved by Adam Pearce and signed by Triple H and himself. Reed came out alone, signed it and said he was there to dethrone The Ruler, not to compete. Once Reed left, Femi said, "Welcome back, Bronson Reed, and good luck. You're gonna need it."Dragon Lee vs. Big CassBackstage, Dragon Lee told Jackie Redmond he felt great while WWE Hall of Famer Rey Mysterio praised his path, until Big Cass promised to stomp out his fire. In the ring, Lee opened with a dropkick and a tope con hilo, but Cass answered with a big boot and two chokeslams on the apron. Lee clawed back with corner dropkicks, a hurricanrana and a torpedo suicide dive. A roll-up stole him the win. Afterward, he hopped the barricade, sat in a fan's lap and sipped a beer while Cass fumed.Winner: Dragon LeeIYO SKY vs. Lyra ValkyriaThe matchup came together earlier in the day. IYO SKY was talking with Raw General Manager Adam Pearce when Lyra Valkyria interrupted, unhappy that beating Bayley had not opened more doors for her. Pearce answered by booking her against Sky that night. The two argued on the spot, and the exchange aired as a video package on the broadcast. Valkyria wanted opportunities, and now she had one in front of her. After the intense fight, SKY secured the win.Winner: IYO SKYThe Judgment Day vs. Je'Von Evans and PentaThe tag match started as a hallway argument. Je'Von Evans told Penta he would become the youngest Money in the Bank winner, and "Dirty" Dominik Mysterio and JD McDonagh cut in. Mysterio claimed Penta had stolen his spot in the Money in the Bank match and said he would have won if Adam Pearce had not gotten in his way. Evans fired back with a joke about Mysterio's heart and McDonagh's head. Penta then offered to team with Evans that night if The Judgment Day wanted another fight.Penta and Evans dominated the stretch with rapid strikes, stereo superkicks and high-flying offense, keeping Mysterio under constant pressure. articles.title: PT Usha’s 42-year reign ends: How Vithya Ramraj finally broke India’s 400m hurdles mark
articles.summary: Bengaluru: For more than four decades, PT Usha’s 55.42 seconds remained the gold standard for India’s women’s 400m hurdlers.
articles.body: Bengaluru: For more than four decades, PT Usha’s 55.42 seconds remained the gold standard for India’s women’s 400m hurdlers. Very few athletes matched her class, and even fewer had the grit to put in the hard yards and challenge the magical number, while many others simply found it insurmountable.Even as the new millennium dawned, India’s top women hurdlers struggled to dip below the one-minute mark. That time was clocked at the 1984 Los Angeles Olympics, when Usha lost the bronze by milliseconds.Asian Games Full Coverage | Schedule | Medal TallyIt was an achievement that put her on the same pedestal as ‘Flying Sikh’ Milkha Singh, who also came close to a bronze in the men’s 400m at the 1960 Rome Olympics.As India enters the cycle for the 2028 Los Angeles Games, the national mark which became nearly permanent has been erased. Fittingly, the ‘Payyoli Express’ has been overtaken by the Coimbatore Super Fast.Vithya Ramraj had earlier equalled the mark three years ago in the heats at the Hangzhou Asiad."I knew she would peak in this competition. I was almost sure that she would do sub 54.5, but it was 54.7. But it is okay because, without progression, you cannot perform at that big level. Atthe Delhi meet on Sep 10,she fell down from a hurdle;otherwise, we were expecting around 55s there and then the progression from there (to the National record).”When asked why it took so long for Usha’s record to be erased, experts agreed that Usha had set the bar very high, very early in a highly demanding event.“The time clocked in 1984 was world class. PT Usha was a generational talent and she had the talent to go even faster. Then we hardly had athletes of that calibre,” said noted coach PB Jaikumar.Jaikumar trained Anu Raghavan for many years, leading to her winning the bronze at the 2010 Asiad. The 33-year-old, returning to the Asiad after a 14-year gap, clocked her personal best time of 55.88s in Nagoya and finished a creditable fifth on Monday.“It’s a highly technical event, where you need both speed and the technique to fly over the 10 hurdles. We have produced very few athletes of Usha’s calibre over the decades, which is why the record stood for so long,” added Jaikumar.Experts also felt that the athletics federation’s focus on making a quality 4x400m relay squad was another reason for the record to stay for so long.“We had quite a few top-class 400m runners but very few of them did well in the individual events like the 400m or 400m hurdles. The moment they began to impress, coaches eyed including them in the relay squad and over the years, priorities shifted from individual events to the relay,” another national coach said.Still way behindJaikumar also said India still has a long way to catch up with the current world standards despite lowering the record below 55 seconds.“It’s a big feat to break a 42-year-old record but you can’t read too much into it. The new record will still place Vithya among the 35-40 fastest in the world. That shows how far we have to catch up. The main takeaway should be the confidence for our athletes that all records can be broken, provided they keep working hard.“We know our athletes don’t stand much of a chance in the Olympics, so we should target the Asian Games. We should train in such a way that our athletes achieve their personal best at these Games. Count how many of our athletes achieved their personal bests at these Games. Count how many of our athletes achieved their personal bests in Nagoya,” Jaikumar signed off.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Murali Sreeshankar twists ankle, refuses wheelchair and returns to win Asian Games silver
articles.summary: Nagoya: The image of Indian long jump ace Murali Sreeshankar twisting his ankle on his fourth jump on a rain-swept Monday night at the Mizuho Park
articles.body: Nagoya: The image of Indian long jump ace Murali Sreeshankar twisting his ankle on his fourth jump on a rain-swept Monday night at the Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium will be a tough one to forget.As the 27-year-old landed awkwardly on his right leg and writhed in pain, memories of the ruptured left patellar tendon that ruled him out of the Paris Olympics and kept him out of the sandpit for almost two years came flooding back. He limped out with the help of medical staff and was offered a wheelchair, which he refused. Even when the medical team advised him not to return, he shrugged them off.Asian Games Full Coverage | Schedule | Medal TallyHe did not need to take his next two attempts. He had already breached the eight-metre mark with his second jump of 8.07m, enough to fetch him silver and a repeat of his podium finish from the previous edition. China’s Yuhao Shi, with a season’s best of 8.17m, took gold. The other Indian in the field, Solomon Patturaj (7.70m), finished seventh.Once his medal was confirmed, Sreeshankar, who won silver at the Glasgow Commonwealth Games, limped over to collect the Indian flag, wrapped himself in the tricolour and celebrated briefly before heading off for treatment.It was a productive day for India in athletics, with the team picking up three silver and three bronze medals.Podium in javelinThe javelin competition was without Neeraj Chopra, but India did not miss out on a podium finish. In fact, there were two.Yashvir Singh saved his best for last, clinching silver with a season’s best of 85.72m. Fancied Sri Lankan Rumesh Pathirage, in red-hot form, continued his rich vein of form to take gold with 88.55m, while Rohit Yadav completed the podium with 84.35m.Olympic champion Arshad Nadeem from Pakistan, who is going through a lean patch, managed an underwhelming 80.29m, which was incidentally his season’s best.Pathirage, who has breached the 90m mark three times this year, took some time to find his rhythm in the testing conditions, allowing Yashvir to take the lead. But with his fourth attempt of 88.33m, the 23-year-old Sri Lankan moved ahead and only got better from there.Double silver for GulveerGulveer Singh, who won silver in the 10,000m three days ago, returned to claim another silver in the 1500m with a personal best of 3:36.72.Gulveer never fell behind in the race and briefly took the lead at the 200m bend, but Japan’s Kazuto Iizawa produced a late burst in the home stretch to take gold in a Games record 3:36.35.Gulveer later admitted he had not paced the race well enough.“I wanted to do better, but I’m glad I could win a medal. I was pacing according to the long-distance running, but he (Iizawa) took off and I couldn’t keep pace,” said the 28-year-old.Parul makes it two in two daysParul Chaudhary, who took silver in the 3000m steeplechase on Saturday, delivered another strong performance to settle for bronze in the 5000m.Parul looked set for silver but could not produce the final push and clocked 15:14.61.The day’s biggest disappointment came in the men’s 3000m steeplechase, where defending champion Avinash Sable finished fourth in 8:21.67. Sable, returning from injury and having said he was peaking for the Games, looked off the pace for much of the race.There was also heartbreak for the women’s 4x100m relay team, which finished fourth despite clocking a season’s best. The quartet of Abinaya Rajarajan, Sneha Sathyanarayana, Sudeshna Shivankar and Tamanna timed 43.57 seconds.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Neeru Dhanda leads India to women’s trap team silver at Asian Games
articles.summary: Neeru Dhanda produced a composed and consistent display on the range to lead India to a silver medal in the women’s trap team event at the Asian Games
articles.body: Neeru Dhanda produced a composed and consistent display on the range to lead India to a silver medal in the women’s trap team event at the Asian Games here on Tuesday.Neeru, Aashima Ahlawat and Manisha Keer combined for 328 points to finish second behind China, which won gold with 346. Kuwait took bronze with 325.The medal was built around a strong individual showing from Neeru, who finished the qualification round with 118 hits out of 125. She was joint-first in the individual standings and also qualified for the individual final.Neeru began with 24 hits in the opening round and followed it with a perfect 24 in the second round. It is also India's second Asian Games medal in the women's trap team event, after the silver won at Hangzhou in 2023 by Manisha Keer, Rajeshwari Kumari and Preeti Rajak.The medal also takes India's shooting haul at the 2026 Asian Games to 13 medals, while India's overall tally moves to 46 medals.But the immediate focus will now turn to Neeru. articles.summary: Sri Lankan javelin thrower Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage said he missed seeing Neeraj Chopra compete at the Asian Games, describing the Indian star's absence
articles.body: Sri Lankan javelin thrower Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage said he missed seeing Neeraj Chopra compete at the Asian Games, describing the Indian star's absence as "bad luck" after an ankle injury forced him out of the continental event.Chopra, a two-time Olympic medallist, was unable to defend the Asian Games men's javelin gold he won in the previous edition in China after suffering an ankle ligament tear during training last month.Asian Games Full Coverage | Schedule | Medal TallyPathirage made the most of Chopra's absence, producing a winning throw of 88.55m with his sixth and final attempt to claim gold at the rain-affected Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium on Monday.India's Yashvir Singh, who replaced the injured Chopra in the athletics team, took silver with a personal best of 85.72m, while Rohit Yadav secured bronze with 84.35m."Yeah, he had a little injury on the ankle after Lausanne Diamond League. It's his bad luck," the 23-year-old Pathirage told PTI when asked if he was missing Chopra after the event."I do sometimes speak to him (Chopra)," he added.Pathirage and Chopra's changing fortunesPathirage and Chopra have shared the field at major competitions, with the Indian also inviting the Sri Lankan to compete at the inaugural NC Classic javelin competition in Bengaluru in July last year.Chopra won that event with a throw of 86.18m, while Pathirage finished third with 84.34m.The results have been very different this year.Pathirage has won all three competitions in which Chopra competed. He began by winning the Doha Diamond League in June, where Chopra finished fourth. The Sri Lankan then claimed gold at the Glasgow Commonwealth Games, with Chopra taking silver.The pattern continued at the Lausanne Diamond League in August, where Pathirage finished first and Chopra was second.Pathirage has also been in remarkable form throughout the season, recording three throws beyond 90m. He has finished first in 13 of the 14 events he has competed in this year, with a second-place finish in the remaining competition.His list of titles includes four Diamond League meetings, the Diamond League Final, World Athletics Ultimate Championships, Commonwealth Games and now the Asian Games.Despite the dominance, Pathirage insisted there was no elaborate secret behind his success."No secret, just normal training every year," he said when asked about his form and three 90m-plus throws this season.'Yashvir and Rohit are very good'Pathirage also praised the two Indian throwers who shared the podium with him in Chopra's absence."Yashvir and Rohit are very good. His average throw has been 85m. Maybe, I think, next year, Yashvir and Rohit can produce big throws for India."The result completed a South Asian sweep of the men's javelin medals at both the Commonwealth Games and Asian Games.For Pathirage, however, the winning throw fell short of what he had hoped to achieve."The conditions were not good due to rain.""I could not get proper grip of my javelin. I had wanted to break the Games record and Asian record but I could not go for my massive throws like 90m."But I am happy to be the first-ever Sri Lankan javelin throw gold medal winner at the Asian Games."World Championships and LA Olympics nextPathirage has already turned his attention towards his next major targets."My next target is World Championship next year and then 2028 LA Olympics."The Sri Lankan made his World Championships debut last year but believes he will enter the next edition with greater experience."I competed for the first time in the World Championships last year, when I had less experience. articles.title: AFCON qualifiers: Wissa guides DR Congo to win, Tunisia held by Botswana
articles.summary: Democratic Republic of the Congo secure their second straight win in Group E, with striker Yoanne Wissa scoring again.
articles.body:
Yoane Wissa scored the first goal and created the second as the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) spoiled a Zimbabwe homecoming by winning a 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifier 2-1 in Harare.

The 30-year-old Newcastle United striker struck in the 30th minute, poking a loose ball into the net after goalkeeper Elvis Chipezeze allowed a cross to slip from his grasp in the qualifying match on Monday.

DRC, who secured a historic last-32 finish at the 2026 FIFA World Cup , went further ahead in first-half added time when a Wissa pass sent Samuel Moutoussamy through to score.

After being outplayed in the opening half by a team 89 places higher in the FIFA world rankings, Zimbabwe improved after half-time, with Marshall Munetsi scoring a 93rd-minute consolation goal.

Zimbabwe last played at home in November 2021 before the Harare venue was deemed unsuitable for international fixtures, leading to lengthy renovations.

DRC, whose second of two AFCON titles came 52 years ago, top Group E with a maximum six points after launching their campaign with a 2-0 home victory over Equatorial Guinea.

Zimbabwe and Equatorial Guinea, who meet twice in November, have three points each, and Sierra Leone are pointless.

A first-minute goal from Loren Zuniga earned Equatorial Guinea a 1-0 win over Sierra Leone in Cameroon’s capital, Yaounde.

Equatorial Guinea are among the 11 of the 48 qualifiers for the AFCON group stage who must host matches at neutral venues as they lack an international-standard stadium.

Central African Republic are another “homeless” nation. They fell 1-0 to Burkina Faso in Group F in the Moroccan commercial hub of Casablanca. Aboubacar Camara netted the second-half winner.

Struggling Tunisia were held at home for the second time in four days, drawing 2-2 with Botswana in Rades near Tunis.

Tunisia looked set for a first competitive win this year when Hazem Mastouri scored either side of half-time after Botswana had taken the lead.

But the minnows from Southern Africa – 90 places below Tunisia in the world rankings – equalised on the hour through a delicate lob from substitute Lebogang Ditsele.

It was the second successive 2-2 draw for Botswana after sharing the points in Libya last week, and they remain top of Group H on goals scored ahead of Tunisia.

articles.title: Vuelve la acción a Premier Padel con un posible enfrentamiento entre Lebrón y Galán en Rotterdam
articles.standfirst: El gaditano y el madrileño se cruzarían en semifinales, mientras las número uno evitan de nuevo a Claudia y Martina
articles.summary: El gaditano y el madrileño se cruzarían en semifinales, mientras las número uno evitan de nuevo a Claudia y Martina
articles.body: Tras dos semanas de descanso justo después del Major de París, uno de los torneos más importantes de la temporada, vuelve la acción a Premier Padel con el P2 de Rotterdam, que junta de nuevo a las mejores parejas del planeta. Con el número uno, las posiciones de privilegio y los billetes al Tour Finals todavía en juego, la moqueta azul de la ciudad neerlandesa servirá para seguir dictaminando los grandes vencedores de esta temporada. Tapia y Coello, que levantaron el título en Roland Garros tras una remontada espectacular en el tercer set, tienen un camino lleno de obstáculos hacia la final. Debutarán ante Edu Alonso y Aimar Goñi en octavos de final. Una dupla que siempre pone las cosas complicadas y que busca dar la sorpresa después de la convocatoria del navarro al Mundial con España. En cuartos, se medirían hipotéticamente a Javi Leal y Fran Guerrero, que vienen de ganar el FIP Platinum de Lyon y que ya les eliminaron en Pretoria. Por su mismo lado del cuadro van Paquito Navarro y Martín Di Nenno, contra los que se cruzarían en semifinales. El sevillano y el argentino buscan defender su cuarto puesto en esta gira europea, pero deberán hacer como mínimo mejores resultados que Jon Sanz y Franco Stupaczuk, que están en la otra parte. ‘Renga’ y el ‘Huracán’, en cambio, están emparejados con Momo González y Lucas Campagnolo en cuartos de final. Quienes sí se verían las caras por un billete a la final son Juan Lebrón y Ale Galán. Desde Londres no se han vuelto a enfrentar, pero tampoco será fácil para ellos. El ‘Alien’, junto a Fede Chingotto, debutará en octavos ante Jensen y Gala para luego tener un hipotético duelo con Stupa y Jon Sanz. No se pueden permitir fallar si quieren seguir optando al liderato del ranking. Por su parte, el ‘Lobo’ y Augsburger cayeron en semifinales en París y buscan acercarse de nuevo a los títulos. Su estreno sería contra Arce y Tello, un primer plato realmente duro en Rotterdam, que a priori no es el torneo que más les conviene por condiciones. Ya en cuartos tendrían a Coki Nieto y Mike Yanguas, que vienen de no brillar en Roland Garros, pero sí de hacer una gesta brutal en Madrid. Habrá que ver cómo vuelven del parón los de Silingo. En el femenino, la principal noticia es la ausencia de Tamara Icardo. La valenciana no pudo estar en París y parece que no ha llegado a tiempo para recuperarse de las molestias físicas y estar disponible en Rotterdam. Su compañera, en cambio, no se queda en casa: Claudia Jensen jugará con la jovencísima Claudia Escacena. Una unión circunstancial que no la hace salirse del top 8. En cuanto a los cuadros, Gemma Triay y Delfi Brea van por el lado de Ari Sánchez y Andrea Ustero, las vencedoras en Roland Garros. Las de Seba Nerone se cruzarían con Salazar y Osoro en cuartos de final, mientras que la dupla catalana aparece con Guinart y Alonso en esa misma ronda. Por el otro lado, Claudia Fernández y Martina Calvo vuelven a estar junto a Paula Josemaría y Bea González. La malagueña y la extremeña volverían a medirse a quienes precisamente las eliminaron en tierras francesas: Sofía Araújo y Marta Ortega. Una posible revancha tras dos semanas en busca de un billete a semifinales. Las ‘Supernenas’, en cambio, debutan ante Goenaga y Caldera para luego tener un posible cruce con Jensen y Escacena o Rufo e Iglesias.

articles.title: Raúl Varela señala a su favorito para el Balón de Oro: "El Mundial pesará más"
articles.standfirst: El presentador de La Tribu apuesta por Luis de la Fuente y destaca sus méritos por delante del resto de candidatos
articles.summary: El presentador de La Tribu apuesta por Luis de la Fuente y destaca sus méritos por delante del resto de candidatos
articles.body: Raúl Varela tiene claro quién reúne más méritos para conquistar el próximo Balón de Oro. El presentador de La Tribu defendió la candidatura de Luis de la Fuente y puso especialmente en valor el Mundial conquistado por España. "Y Luis de la Fuente también lo pide. El Balón de Oro. Y bien que hace porque además de todos los candidatos no sólo en la categoría de entrenadores sino también de jugadores seguramente es en el que más méritos concurren para llevarse semejante galardón", aseguró Varela. El periodista considera que conseguir el premio supondría poner el broche a "una carrera fantástica labrada a base de buen comportamiento y mayor conocimiento y acierto". Además, destacó la naturalidad con la que el seleccionador presentó su candidatura: "A De la Fuente le preguntaron ayer y con su habitual naturalidad levantó la mano y se sumó al carro de los que quieren ir a Londres a recoger esa pelota bañada en color dorado". Varela reconoció el trabajo realizado por otros entrenadores, pero cree que el éxito de España puede terminar decantando la balanza. "La temporada nos ha dejado nombres de otros técnicos con trabajos estupendos y logros fantásticos pero seguramente el Mundial y la forma de conseguirlo pesará más que cualquier liga doméstica o incluso la segunda Champions consecutiva de Luis Enrique". También reivindicó todo lo conseguido por De la Fuente al frente de la selección: "Los títulos, los números, su proceder y esa forma de defender, fomentar y poner en valor en este caso al futbolista español". "Ha logrado un consenso casi unánime en lo que a las convocatorias y alineaciones se refieren, apenas está contestado, sublima el método de trabajo implantado en Las Rozas desde hace lustros y su forma de ejercer de portavoz y embajador nunca nos deja en mal lugar", añadió. Varela también hizo referencia a ese componente de fortuna que suele acompañar a los campeones. "Además, sí, tiene esa dosis de suerte que los campeones necesitan, aunque suele decirse que forma parte del trabajo diario. Se autoexpulsa Enzo, se lesiona Courtois, Dani Olmo la saca bajo palos". El periodista espera que la dinámica de España continúe durante octubre, aunque recordó las dudas de De la Fuente con el nuevo calendario de la Nations por "el hecho de jugar cuatro partidos en menos de dos semanas con el consiguiente riesgo de lesiones y los líos añadidos con los clubes". "Aquello de Lamine y Flick le dejó bastante escaldado", apuntó. Varela cerró su defensa del seleccionador con una sentencia: "De la Fuente levantó la mano. Hizo bien. En realidad debería levantar las dos, pero con el trofeo bien agarrado"

articles.title: Asian Games: South Korea volleyball team latest to be taken to wrong venue
articles.summary: Transporting athletes to the wrong location has emerged as a recurring issue at the Asian Games in Japan.
articles.body:
South Koreans were victims of another Asian Games transport mix-up in Japan when the bus carrying their men’s volleyball team went to a venue an hour away from where they were supposed to go.

South Korea’s volleyball players were forced to cancel their training on Monday morning before the group game against Taiwan later in the day following the latest logistical issue.

“An organiser-provided shuttle bus took our team to Okazaki instead of its training venue in Inuyama yesterday morning,” an official from the Korea Volleyball Association told the AFP news agency on Tuesday.

“With too much time lost to turn back, the training was cancelled. We lodged a formal complaint to the organisers through the KSOC,” the official added, referring to South Korea’s Olympic committee.

The volleyball team went on to beat Taiwan 3-1.

Repeated organisational failures at the games in Aichi-Nagoya have left athletes frustrated, with accommodation and transport for more than 17,000 athletes and officials among the main issues .

South Korea’s men’s basketball team were forced to miss training ahead of their final against Japan last week when their bus failed to turn up. The gaffe did not affect their results as they went on to win the title.

Also on Monday, Pakistan’s men’s volleyball players were bussed to the wrong arena for their match against Uzbekistan, delaying it by 45 minutes.

“This is another mismanagement by Japan at the ongoing Asian Games,” Pakistan captain Murad Jehan said from the bus in an Instagram video.

A spokesperson for the local organising committee said the Pakistani and South Korean teams had departed from the same accommodation and there was “an error in matching teams to vehicles”.

“Each boarded a bus heading to the wrong destination. We sincerely apologise to both teams for the inconvenience,” she said.

“We caused great inconvenience, and the organising committee takes this seriously,” the spokesperson added.

“It is basic, but we will again make sure boarding teams and vehicle destinations are properly checked and displayed, and work to prevent a recurrence.”

articles.summary: From being inspired by her cousin Lakhsay Sheron’s Asian Games medal to winning one herself, Neeru Dhanda has completed a remarkable journey - and in the
articles.body: From being inspired by her cousin Lakhsay Sheron’s Asian Games medal to winning one herself, Neeru Dhanda has completed a remarkable journey - and in the process, created a piece of history for Indian shooting.The 26-year-old Indian shooter produced a stunning 28/30 in the women’s trap final to clinch gold at the Asian Games on Tuesday. China’s Sun Yunong finished second with 26, while Kuwait’s Hajar Abdulmalik took bronze with 21.Dhanda’s 28 also shattered the previous Asian record of 24. The Indian had already announced her intent by topping qualification with 118 hits out of 125, and she carried that form into the six-shooter final to produce the biggest result of her career in the process delivering India its first individual gold medal of the 2026 Games and taking the country’s tally to five gold medals and 47 overall.Earlier in the day, Dhanda had already played a central role in India’s women’s trap team silver, joining Aashima Ahlawat and Manisha Keer to finish second behind China.For Dhanda, the triumph comes just months after she broke new ground at the ISSF World Cup in Lonato, Italy. In July, she became the first Indian woman to win an individual gold medal in trap at an ISSF World Cup.Asian Games Full Coverage|Medal Tally|ScheduleThe Asian Games gold now gives that World Cup success a continental dimension. Dhanda had arrived in Aichi-Nagoya as the reigning Asian champion, having won gold at the 2025 Asian Shooting Championships. She also had a mixed-team bronze from the ISSF World Cup in Almaty earlier this year.From tin cans to the Indian Army and World Cup gloryDhanda was inspired to take up shooting after watching her maternal cousin Lakshay Sheoran win a silver medal in men's trap at the 2018 Asian Games. Sheoran also lent her his gun when she was beginning her journey in the sport. Years later, Dhanda has followed him to the Asian Games podium, but has gone one better by winning gold.The rise has been backed by the Indian Army, where Dhanda serves as a Naib Subedar in the Corps of Military Police. She trains at the Army Marksmanship Unit in Mhow and works with foreign coach Peter Wilson, the London 2012 Olympic trap champion. articles.title: Bombazo: ¡Luke Littler, el 'Messi de los dardos', eliminado en primera ronda del Mundial!
articles.standfirst: El deportista de 19 años y vigente campeón dijo adiós al campeonato ante el veterano Luke Woodhouse
articles.summary: El deportista de 19 años y vigente campeón dijo adiós al campeonato ante el veterano Luke Woodhouse
articles.body: Luke Littler, vigente campeón del mundo y número uno del ranking, quedó eliminado del World Grand Prix tras perder ante el veterano Luke Woodhouse en Leicester. Littler comenzó imponiéndose en el primer set gracias a un checkout de 106 puntos a doble 15, pero Woodhouse reaccionó y terminó llevándose el partido por 2-1, después de ganar el set decisivo por 3-1 en mangas. Las medias reflejaron una noche lejos del mejor nivel de ambos: 82,51 para Woodhouse y 82,41 para Littler. El verdugo del joven inglés, lejos de cebarse con su victoria, salió en su defensa después del partido: "Luke no es un robot, es único. Espero que la gente se tome el tiempo de valorar lo bueno que es y no se lo ponga difícil. Puede que no volvamos a ver a otro Luke Littler". El propio Woodhouse reconoció que el encuentro estuvo lejos de ser brillante. "Es la primera vez que juego contra él en un escenario principal y, qué duda cabe, estaba un poco tembloroso", explicó. "Creo que fue un partido bastante deslucido. Por supuesto, me quedo con la victoria". También admitió que Littler "no estaba funcionando a pleno rendimiento". El campeón del mundo llegaba además después de una semana complicada. En las World Series of Darts Finals de Ámsterdam cayó en cuartos ante Jonny Clayton (10-4), después de acertar solo cuatro de sus 20 lanzamientos a doble. Los abucheos de parte del público neerlandés provocaron entonces su enfado.

articles.title: ¿Qué puede pasar con el precio de la gasolina y el diésel desde este 1 de octubre?
articles.standfirst: Este 30 de septiembre acaban las ayudas a la compra de gasolina y diésel. Esto es lo que puede suceder con los precios en función de que se acaben las ayudas fiscales o se mantengan.
articles.summary: Este 30 de septiembre acaban las ayudas a la compra de gasolina y diésel. Esto es lo que puede pasar con los precios a partir de octubre.
articles.body: Repostar se ha ido encareciendo semana tras semana durante este mes de septiembre, hasta situar el precio medio en nuestro país en unos estratosféricos 1,95 euros/litro para la gasolina y en 1,94 para el diésel. Y el panorama puede empeorar este 1 de octubre, cuando se acabe el paquete de ayudas fiscales que todavía hoy suaviza los precios. La rebaja del Impuesto Especial sobre los Hidrocarburos (IEH) se puso en marcha en marzo de este debido al encarecimiento de la energía provocado por la guerra entre Israel, Estados Unidos e Irán, que trajo consigo el bloqueo del estrecho de Ormuz. Desde entonces se han ido renovando y ajustando varias veces, y la versión que todavía hoy está en vigor se aprobó a finales de junio y fue convalidada por el Congreso el 23 de julio, fijando un calendario de rebajas decrecientes para julio, agosto y septiembre. En la práctica, esa ayuda supone hoy 20 céntimos/litro de descuento en el diésel y 5 céntimos en la gasolina. Que el diésel conserve la rebaja máxima mientras la gasolina ya ha bajado a la mínima se debe a una cláusula prevista de antemano: si la inflación interanual de un carburante supera el 15% en un mes de referencia, la rebaja de ese carburante vuelve a los 20 céntimos sin que el Gobierno tenga que mover un papel. Eso fue lo que pasó con el gasóleo, cuya inflación llegó al 15,7% en julio, mientras que la gasolina se quedó en un porcentaje inferior y siguió el calendario de descenso en las ayudas hasta los 5 céntimos actuales. Pero ese mecanismo automático dejará de estar en vigor este 30 de septiembre. Es decir, que desde este jueves la rebaja no se prorrogará sola, sino que hará falta que el Gobierno apruebe una nueva norma que la mantenga, la modifique... o la deje caer. De momento, la patronal de gasolineras Agrupación Española de Vendedores al por menor de Carburantes y Combustibles (AEVECAR) ha reclamado esta semana al Ministerio de Economía que reactive de forma urgente las herramientas fiscales que ya funcionaron entre marzo y junio, además de una rebaja adicional y transitoria del propio impuesto especial. Desde AEVECAR aseguran que, si no hay ninguna medida antes del jueves, la gasolina podría subir 6,05 céntimos por litro y el diésel hasta 24,20 céntimos, sumando en ambos casos la pérdida de la bonificación y el IVA. Pero no se puede echar solo la culpa a los impuestos, porque en esta subida también ha influido la escalada del precio del petróleo en los mercados internacionales y, sobre todo, el encarecimiento de los productos ya refinados (gasolina y gasóleo). De nuevo, el origen de esto último sigue siendo el conflicto en Oriente Medio, que ha reducido el tráfico de crudo por el estrecho de Ormuz y ha tensionado también la capacidad de refino disponible en Europa. ¿Puede suceder en España como ya pasa en Francia, donde muchas gasolineras están quedándose sin combustible? Según ha reconocido el propio Gobierno francés, en torno al 14% de sus gasolineras presenta escasez al menos de un carburante, un porcentaje que llegó a rozar el 17% hace unos días y que se concentra, en nueve de cada diez casos, en estaciones de TotalEnergies. Ahora bien, esto tiene una causa, y es que esta petrolera decidió poner un tope máximo a sus precios y esto hizo que se multiplicara la demanda en sus estaciones. Además, desde nuestro país se considera que este caso no es extrapolable a España porque aquí tenemos ocho refinerías en lugar de las cinco que tienen en Francia. Con la incertidumbre sobre si el Gobierno tomará una medida a última hora para amortiguar o contener la subida, lo más prudente a día de hoy sería llenar el depósito antes de acabe el mes. En un coche de gasolina con un depósito de 55 litros esto supondría ahorrar unos 3,30 euros si se acaban las ayudas, mientras que el ahorro para un coche diésel con la misma capacidad podría ascender a unos 13,30 euros. Si por el contrario se mantuvieran las ayudas, los precios seguirían en rangos similares a los actuales.

Llenar el depósito supone cada día un esfuerzo económico mayor. Magnific.
En Francia, algunas estaciones se están quedando sin gasolina o diésel. Magnific.

articles.title: September surprises highlight our South Shore football rankings
articles.summary: Hull, North Quincy and Pembroke are off to undefeated starts following down years.
articles.body:
Through Week 3 of the high school football season , a major theme on the South Shore has been the bounce back season.

Hull, North Quincy and Pembroke are off to eye-raising 3-0 starts. Those teams combined to go 11-21 last season and the Pirates have already matched their 2025 win total (Pembroke and NQ both finished 4-7). Whitman-Hanson just picked up its second win on Friday after going 1-10 last fall.

With September about to be in the rear-view mirror, now the road will get tougher in October. League play kicks off this week and those September surprises won't be able to sneak up on anybody as Halloween nears.

On the bubble: Bridgewater-Raynham (1-2), Cohasset (1-2), Hanover (1-2), Hingham (2-1), Middleboro (2-1), Norwell (2-1), Oliver Ames (2-1), Quincy (2-1), Silver Lake (2-1), West Bridgewater (2-1), Whitman-Hanson (2-1)

Record and last week's ranking in parenthesis.

Hull High football pulls out win against Boston English

The Pirates matched their 2025 win total by pulling out a gritty 13-8 win over Boston English on Friday. Hull is on the second week of a five-game homestand. The Oct. 9 game against South Shore Tech will have major playoff implications for both teams.

The Wildcats fell to undefeated Newton North 14-12 last week in a game that came down to the wire. Weymouth opens Bay State Herget Division with a pair of winnable games against Wellesley and Braintree.

The Dragons shook off a Week 1 loss to Scituate with notable wins over Hanover and Barnstable. Duxbury's win over Barnstable last week was one of the best wins in the entire state.

Big win over Sandwich gives Pembroke a rare 3-0 start to season

The Titans took care of business in September, now we'll find out where they stand in a loaded Patriot League Fisher Division. Next up is a hungry Hanover squad that shook off an 0-2 start to get a notable win over West Bridgewater last week.

The Raiders have been demons in the defensive backfield, intercepting seven passes already. Quarterback Cole Doyle leads a pass-happy offense. Next up is a trip to Somerville, which boosts a 2-1 record, before Patriot League play starts.

A week after rival Weymouth narrowly escaped with a 10-7 win over Diman, Milton took it to the Bengals on Friday. Milton defeated Diman 41-0 and has bounced back in style following a 42-25 loss to Marshfield in the opener.

Marshfield High football wins wild one against Bridgewater-Raynham

The Rams get a well-deserved week off following a really tough September slate. After seeing a 15-0 fourth-quarter lead evaporate against Bridgewater-Raynham on Thursday, Mikey Appel kicked the winning field goal as time expired to send the Rams to some time off on a high note.

The Blue Devils have won 15 games in a row and took care of business in September by outscoring foes 92-18. The schedule gets a lot tougher in October and that starts this Friday with a home game against Cohasset. Both teams won Super Bowl crowns last season.

On a pound-for-pound level, nobody has had a more impressive start than the Green Wave. Abington owns wins over Div. 4 Longmeadow, Div. 3 Hingham and fellow Div. 6 contender. One of the biggest games of the year is coming up this week against Norwell. That game is the area's only showdown on Thursday.

Another week, another dominant Grayson Foley outing. Foley scored four touchdowns and ran for 223 yards in a 42-21 win over Marblehead. The Sailors open Patriot League Fisher Division play against a battle-tested Plymouth South squad.

articles.summary: Week 6 football highlights ― Benedictine, Savannah Country Day and Effingham County were among the winners under the lights on Friday, Sept. 26.
articles.body:
Week 6 of the high school football season in the Greater Savannah area had a number of plot lines that kept fans entertained on Friday, Sept. 25.

Savannah Country Day got a big-time two-way performance from quarterback Devin Trawick as the Hornets went on the road to edge Bethesda and end the Blazers 15-game win streak.

Here are the scores and highlights of the games involving Savannah area schools on Friday, September 25.

Benedictine went on the road and edged Richmond Academy in a Region 1-5A matchup.

BC lost a fumble in the final minutes, but the Cadet defense buckled down for a stop on a 4th and 6 on their own 35 on a pass breakup by Jon Black.

BC quarterback Omari Burse was 20 of 28 passing for 293 yards and pair of touchdowns and rushed for 74 yards and two scores.

Purdue commit Eron Mallard had 11 receptions for 141 yards and a score and rushed for 29 yards and a touchdown.

Senior Stanley Smart Jr., who has committed to Virginia Tech, ran for 150 yards and two touchdowns.

Richmond Academy quarterback Carson Hand was 16 of 27 passing for 336 yards with three touchdowns and an interception for the Muskateers (4-1).

BC (4-1) will host Evans (3-2) on Friday, Oct. 2, in a Region 1-5 matchup at Memorial Stadium.

Bethesda, the defending SCISA Class 2A state champion, saw its 15-game winning streak come to an end in a back-and-forth battle against visiting Savannah Country Day.

SCD quarterback Devin Trawick was 9 of 17 passing for 238 yards with two touchdowns and two interceptions and ran for 41 yards on nine carries. Hornet senior Thomas Holland ran for 99 yards on 23 attempts.

Sophomore receiver Amir Atkinson had four catches for 167 yards and two scores for the Hornets (2-5).

Holland led SCD with 14 tackles at linebacker and Trawick added five tackles with a pair of interceptions ― one returned for a score.

Bethesda's Jordan Turner was 12 of 23 passing for 98 yards with two interceptions and ran for 204 yards and a pair of scores, including an 80-yard touchdown run.

Ka'Mond Young led Bethesda with 14 tackles and a pair of sacks.

Bethesda (3-1) will play at Camden Military (0-4) on Friday, Oct. 2. SCD has a bye before playing at Bulloch Academy (6-1) on Oct. 9.

Host Calvary Day improved to 4-1 on the season with a non-region win over Rockdale County.

Senior quarterback James Mobley IV was 16 of 23 passing for 307 yards and three touchdowns.

Marlon Knight Jr. had five receptions for 83 yards and a score, Ty Pinckney had two catches for 79 yards and a touchdown and Jalen Hicks had a scoring catch. Jonathan Perry had four receptions for 98 yards for the Cavs.

Ca'Den Jones led the Cavs with 85 yards rushing and a score on 15 carries.

Calvary Day is set to play at Metter (0-5) on Friday, Oct. 2.

Host Effingham County's explosive offense was the key as the Rebels beat Bradwell in a Region 1-6A shootout.

Sophomore quarterback Matthew Dillon completed all eight of his passes for 144 yards with scoring strikes to Trayvis Hunter and Isaiah Brown.

The Rebels racked up 408 yards rushing as Jmere Doe-Davis had 205 yards and three touchdowns on 17 carries and junior Jordan Mydell rushed for a 209 yards and three scores on 31 carries. It was a career-high yardage total for Mydell, whose previous best was an 83-yard performance in a win over Evans last week.

Senior Jah'barri Felix was 11 of 19 passing for 210 yards with four touchdowns and an interception for Bradwell (3-2).

His classmate, Cameron Keeve, rushed for 135 yards and a score on 11 carries and had three catches for 88 yards and a touchdown. Carlito Savea had four catches for 76 yards and a score and Jacobi Pasley and Tyson Spears also had scoring grabs for the Tigers.

Bradwell Institute is set to play at Brunswick ( ) in a region game on Friday, Oct. 2, while Effingham County (3-2), which is averaging 43 points a game, is set to play at Glynn Academy (2-3).

articles.title: Klopp would be first Germany coach to fail to win first three games
articles.summary: Jürgen Klopp would become the first Germany men's coach to fail to win in his first three games in charge if his side do not beat Serbia in Thursday's Nation...
articles.body:
Jürgen Klopp would become the first Germany men's coach to fail to win in his first three games in charge if his side do not beat Serbia in Thursday's Nations League game in Munich.

The 59-year-old has so far recorded a 1-1 draw in the Netherlands and a 1-0 home defeat against Greece.

But there are good omens for Klopp given two successful predecessors - Sepp Herberger and Helmut Schön - also went their first two games winless before securing a victory in their third.

Herberger then led Germany to their first World Cup title in 1954. Schön is the only Germany men's coach to win both the European Championship (1972) and World Cup (1974).

After defeat on his home debut against Greece on Sunday, Klopp laughed off talk of negative records.

"Better a bad start than a bad ending," he said.

articles.title: Watch: Titans' Brian Daboll is frustrated by Giants' game-sealing pick
articles.summary: Tennessee Titans offensive coordinator Brian Daboll showed his frustrations after a costly late interception.
articles.body:
The Tennessee Titans again struggled against the New York Giants , with the most glaring issue being an offense that didn't show up until the second half in a 12-7 loss. Yes, Cam Ward and the offense came to life in the second half to make it close, but two failed trips into the red zone cost them the game.

While the first trip, a failed fourth-down pass attempt into the end zone, hurt, that pain is nothing compared to the last-second interception Cam Ward threw in the end zone with 17 seconds remaining. And from the look of it, offensive coordinator Brian Daboll was not happy with his decision.

At that moment, Tennessee had two timeouts remaining and could have easily lived to fight another down, making Ward's decision to force the ball even more questionable. What makes that decision even more head-scratching is that, early in the season, Ward used his legs in that same situation, including a touchdown run against the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 2.

That last-second play was the nail in the coffin, but Daboll's first-half playcalling definitely helped the Titans dig a hole they couldn't get out of, and he should definitely take a look in the mirror. Yes, everyone should be upset at the forced throw and the loss, but there is a lot of blame to go around for an offense that has not been good enough in 2026.

articles.title: Dan Quinn reveals Austin Ekeler's status for Commanders' Week 4 trip to London
articles.summary: Dan Quinn is thrilled to welcome Austin Ekeler back to the Commanders. Will he available for Week 4 in London?
articles.body:
Washington Commanders running back Rachaad White's shoulder injury didn't affect a new signing.

When I first read Monday morning that the Commanders were bringing back running back Austin Ekeler, my first thought was something like, "Uh oh, White's shoulder injury must have flared up much worse after Sunday's game."

Turns out the Commanders actually made this decision to sign Ekeler on Saturday. So the signing wasn't, and couldn't have been, a result of anything that happened in Sunday's 33-31 win over the Seattle Seahawks . Commanders GM Adam Peters and head coach Dan Quinn have clearly been in dialogue, looking for ways to address various issues, and they feel Ekeler has fully recovered and is ready to go.

You recall Ekeler tore his Achilles tendon in a non-contact injury during the Commanders Week 2 game at Green Bay in 2025. Unlike receiver Brandon Aiyuk , Ekeler was not concerned with making videos and selfies on social media during his offseason. The few times we saw Ekeler during the offseason, he was doing mobility work or pumping iron, working to earn one more chance to play in the NFL.

Quinn, on Monday, stated, "Yes, we definitely expect him (Ekeler) to travel (to London) and be a part of it this week. A new system for him on offense. But we'll get him into the mix and see what the next three days look like. It was very cool to have Austin here. A great teammate and one really respected teammate here. So, it was definitely good to have him back in the meeting today. We'll get him into practice and see where it gets into on Thursday and Friday as we get towards the end of the week."

The Commanders currently have Jacory Croskey-Merritt , Rachaad White and Kaytron Allen on the current roster. Signing Ekeler brings the running back total to four. Ekeler provided plenty of offensive fireworks during the 2024 season with quickness as a runner, receiver out of the backfield and kick returner. Ekeler suffered a major concussion injury returning kickoffs.

Ekeler will be 32 next May, and remember, Jeremy McNichols , who will turn 31 in December, was placed on Injured Reserve and will miss at least the first four games.

articles.title: Peoria Rivermen get a high-powered veteran winger, while another announces retirement
articles.summary: The Peoria Rivermen have welcomed back top six forward Mike Gelatt, signed a rookie college forward, and seen the retirement of a beloved player.
articles.body:
PEORIA — The Peoria Rivermen probably thought they were preparing for life after Mike Gelatt in the 2026-27 SPHL season.

But the big, skilled veteran winger became a late returnee Tuesday when he arrived from the ECHL to sign with the Rivermen for a fifth season.

A 6-foot-2, 210-pound right wing, Gelatt is a top six forward in the SPHL, and when healthy and on the ice creates a challenge for opponents to stop in the attacking zone.

"Mike is one of our older guys, you lean on him for leadership, he wants to play the Rivermen way and win games and help his teammates be better," Rivermen head coach Jean-Guy Trudel said. "Any day Mike Gelatt walks into your locker room is a good day. And this is a good day. He understands our culture, he's part of our history and he knows what the goals are here."

Gelatt, 29, is from Middletown, N.J., and was in ECHL Trenton's camp this fall with his younger brother, John.

Mike Gelatt knows that class-AA level well, spending 24 games in the ECHL last season on a call-up with Utah.

He's been an elite player with the Rivermen, playing 90 regular-season games in parts of four seasons, with 38 goals, 43 assists and a +38 rating.

He has played another 28 games for Peoria in SPHL postseason, with seven goals and 14 assists.

Gelatt played junior hockey in the NAHL for parts of three seasons with New Jersey and Wilkes-Barre.

He went on to a college career, playing 63 games with 20 goals and 21 assists for NCAA Div.-III Skidmore College.

He finished his collegiate career with a fifth season, at University of Wisconsin-River Falls, in 2022-23, before turning pro with the Rivermen in the spring.

In 2023-24, his first full pro season, he helped the Rivermen win the SPHL President's Cup championship, netting 11 goals and 16 assists in just 34 games.

The Rivermen have signed rookie forward Everett Pietila .

The 5-foot-10, 185-pounder from Howell, Mich., spent the last two seasons playing NCAA Div.-I hockey for Lake Superior State.

He spent two seasons before that playing junior hockey in the NAHL with Wisconsin.

Fast fact: He is one of nine children in his family.

Popular Rivermen winger Jordan Ernst has announced his retirement from pro hockey, on social media. The popular Rivermen star played 214 regular-season games, with 106 goals, in parts of six seasons. He poured on another 17 goals in 38 playoff games, and was part of the Rivermen President's Cup championship teams in the SPHL in 2021-22 and 2023.24. … The Rivermen released two players from their camp roster Tuesday, including left wing Bohdan Zinchenko and forward Joowon "Timothy" Kim .

articles.body:
West Ottawa boys tennis takes on Holland at home

HOLLAND - When Michael Gorno and Graham Tanis started playing doubles together as freshman, something clicked.

Their strengths matched, the personalities matched and it turned into a successful year.

The duo has been together all four tennis seasons, won a state championship and last week, passed 100 career doubles victories.

"It is a true testament to our success together over the years," Gorno said. "Playing together for four years and having the amount of success that we've had - two times in the state finals and winning a chip is not something a lot of people get to say. It is a blessing."

Reaching 100 victories is extremely difficult for any player because most players play about 30 matches or so a year.

"That is a pretty solid number. I have had a blast playing with Michael for four years," Tanis said. "We are good friends outside of tennis and it is a blessing to play with him."

But reaching 100 wins as doubles players is even more rare since players often move up to singles or lose partners to graduation.

The team has grown into one of the best doubles teams in the state regardless of division.

"Michael has a great forehand, has fun and makes me play better," Tanis said.

"Graham's biggest strength is definitely his serve. He gets double-digit aces just about every match," Gorno said.

"We found some raw success and then toned it down and got a championship at D4. Last year, moving to No. 1 doubles was a big challenge," Gorno said. "This year we are moving so fluidly. We are like one person on the doubles court."

As sophomores they were partners again, winning a Division 4 state championship.

When the Maroons moved back up to Division 3, the duo was again together at No. 1 doubles leading the team to the state tournament and reaching the finals once again.

"Coming up short last year at the state tournament was definitely a bummer," Gorno said. "But senior season, we are ready to compete hard."

"I really want to get back at it at the state tournament and try to catch a 'W' this year," Tanis said. "We will see where we end up - we are just going to keep playing hard."
